hypothesis: A matching 128-thread target block and source tile halves the dynamic shared-memory footprint versus the prior 256-thread variant, while staging only force-relevant source fields reduces each tile to 16 bytes per particle. The smaller tile also doubles CTA count for a given N and doubles the number of tile iterations, so any benefit from reduced resource use or increased CTA availability may be offset by lower source reuse and more barriers; the official measurements must decide.
notes: This is a new configuration and has not been measured. Active and tail threads remain in both block-wide barriers; partial source tiles are bounded, self-interactions use the global source index, and only active targets store output. The force and integration arithmetic order is preserved. Controller correctness and timing results are required before drawing a performance conclusion.
transformations: Use a 128-thread CTA and matching 128-particle source chunks; set items_per_block to 128 to keep the launch configuration compatible and preserve complete target coverage.
Stage only source x, y, z, and mass in a compact shared-memory structure, reserving 2048 dynamic shared-memory bytes per CTA.

Keep one target and one force accumulator per active thread; all threads participate in both barriers, partial source tiles are bounded, self-interactions are excluded by global index, and inactive tail threads do not write output.
